Comment code in my language. Reset Reset everything Go back to the defaults? The style, the settings, the name and your texts will be cleared. Custom Your own mix of the settings below. Default The assistant\'s own calm manner. No fluff Short and to the point, nothing extra. Detailed Thorough, with reasons, examples and structure. Friendly Warm, informal and encouraging. Professional Formal, polished and well organised. Blunt No flattery: says when you are wrong. Mentor Step by step, so that you understand why. Expert Precise terms, code examples, firm advice. Playful Lively and witty, with emoji. Length Short Just the point: the answer and a couple of key things. Normal As the question needs. Detailed In depth: reasons, nuances and details. Explanations Answer Straight to the answer, without how it got there. Normal Explains when it helps. Teach Teaches step by step and says why. Level Beginner Plain words, no jargon, terms explained. Normal Everyday language, terms when needed. Expert Precise terms, no basics. Examples None No examples unless you ask. Normal Examples where they help. Many Concrete examples and short working code. Headings and lists Prose Flowing text, no lists or headings. Normal Lists and headings when they fit. Many Headings, lists, tables and bold accents. Warmth Dry Matter-of-fact, no pleasantries. Normal Calm and polite. Warm Warm and friendly, encouraging. Enthusiasm Level Even, no exclamation marks. Normal Moderate. Lively With spark, glad about your ideas. Formality Casual Informal, everyday words. Normal Neutral. Formal Formal and strict. Humour None No jokes. Normal Now and then, when it fits. Lots Jokes and teases when it fits. Emoji None Not a single emoji. Rarely Rarely, by mood. Often Plenty of emoji, for life. Directness Gentle Gentle: the good first, careful criticism. Normal Honest but tactful. Blunt Blunt: says when you are wrong, no flattery. Own opinion None Shows the options, the choice is yours. Normal Advises when asked. Always Always says what it would pick and why. Clarifying questions Never No questions: assumes and carries on. Normal Asks when there is no way around it. Often Asks first when the task is big or unclear. How do I brew green tea? Happy to help. Oh, let me tell you! I will gladly help. 80 °C, a spoon per cup, 2–3 minutes. Use water at about 80 °C, not boiling, and a teaspoon of leaves per cup. Steep for 2–3 minutes. Green tea Water: about 80 °C, not boiling Tea: 1 tsp per cup Time: 2–3 minutes Boiling water is the usual mistake: it simply ruins the tea. If your tea used to taste bitter, no worries: it is almost always the water. Why not boiling: water that is too hot makes the tea bitter. Why not boiling: at 100 °C tannins leave the leaf fast, and the tea turns bitter. Why not boiling: above 85 °C the extraction of catechins and caffeine jumps, hence the bitterness and astringency. The leaves can be steeped 2–3 more times, adding 30 seconds each time. For example: sencha 1–1.5 minutes, longjing 2–3 minutes. My pick is loose leaf: bags fall clearly short in taste. Loose leaf or bags is a matter of taste: both have their pluses. Save the boiling water for the pasta. What tea do you have, loose or bags? What tea do you have, loose leaf or bags? Enjoy your tea
